# ASAM specification references

Local Markdown copies of the ASAM standards RoadMaker implements, kept in the
repository so **every checkout and every git worktree has them**. They are
reading material for contributors, not part of the build and not shipped in any
artifact.

Generated by [`scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py`](../../scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py)
— **do not hand-edit**. Every file carries a header with its source URL, the
spec version, and the date it was fetched. To refresh:

```sh
python scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py --std opendrive --out third_party/asam
```

## What is here, and what is deliberately not

| Standard | Version | Tracked? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASAM OpenDRIVE | 1.8.1, 1.9.0 | **yes** | carries its own unrestricted licence grant (below) |
| ASAM OpenSCENARIO XML | 1.4.0 | **no** | no comparable grant — see [OpenSCENARIO](#asam-openscenario-not-tracked) |

Start at [`INDEX.md`](INDEX.md) for the chapter map.

## Rights and licence

**These documents are the copyrighted property of ASAM e.V. Robomous claims no
ownership of them, and the Apache-2.0 licence covering the rest of this
repository does not apply to anything under `third_party/asam/`.**

### ASAM OpenDRIVE — tracked

The OpenDRIVE specification carries a licence clause that **replaces** ASAM's
regular terms (§ 2(1) of the [ASAM licensing
terms](https://www.asam.net/license/)) with an unrestricted grant. As published
on the specification itself:

> This document is the copyrighted property of ASAM e.V.
>
> The licensor grants everyone a basic, non-exclusive and unlimited license to
> use the standard ASAM OpenDRIVE.

ASAM OpenDRIVE® is a registered trademark of ASAM e.V.

Sources — the authoritative text always wins over the copies here:

- [ASAM OpenDRIVE 1.8.1 specification](https://publications.pages.asam.net/standards/ASAM_OpenDRIVE/ASAM_OpenDRIVE_Specification/v1.8.1/specification/index.html)
- [ASAM OpenDRIVE 1.9.0 specification](https://publications.pages.asam.net/standards/ASAM_OpenDRIVE/ASAM_OpenDRIVE_Specification/v1.9.0/specification/index.html)

### These copies are converted, and therefore non-normative

The files here are the published HTML **converted to Markdown and repacked into
per-chapter files** for offline reading and searching. That conversion is a
change of form: headings, tables and figures do not always survive it faithfully,
and **figures are not included at all**.

Treat them as a *navigation and search aid*. For anything normative — an exact
enum list, a table's units, a rule id you intend to cite in a diagnostic — read
the published specification at the source URL in the file header. Where the two
disagree, ASAM's publication is correct and the copy here is a conversion
artifact.

### ASAM OpenSCENARIO (not tracked)

The OpenSCENARIO XML specification carries **no equivalent grant**. It falls
under ASAM's regular [licensing terms](https://www.asam.net/license/), which
allow members and purchasers to pass standards on only in narrow circumstances
and give recipients no onward redistribution rights at all. Committing it to a
public repository would put it in the hands of readers who have no licence to
receive it.

So it stays untracked, and `.gitignore` excludes it. Fetch it locally when you
need it:

```sh
python scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py --std openscenario --out third_party/asam
```

This is the same reason RoadMaker has no OpenSCENARIO `.xsd` and validates
exported `.xosc` by [handing it to
esmini](https://github.com/Robomous/RoadMaker/issues/257) instead.

### If ASAM asks

Robomous will remove or replace these copies on request from ASAM e.V. Open an
issue, or contact the maintainer at the address in
[`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE).

## Note for tooling

The repository's Markdown link check globs `docs/**/*.md` and root `*.md`
only — **do not add `third_party/**` to it.** These files are converted from
ASAM's HTML and carry that document's own internal links, which do not resolve
outside their published site; the job would fail on someone else's link
structure rather than on anything RoadMaker controls.

## Why they are tracked at all

They were previously fetched into `.claude/`, which is gitignored — so a fresh
clone or a new `git worktree` had **no specification text**, and a `grep` for a
chapter returned nothing rather than an error. That silently defeated the
project rule that standards behaviour is implemented from the specification and
never from memory ([contributing
workflow](../../docs/contributing/workflow.md), [domain
references](../../docs/domain/references.md)).
